newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares rebound on Sampoerna, secondaries.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares rebound on Sampoerna, secondaries.

text.p: A sharp rise in cigarette-maker Sampoerna and local-led active buying of some secondaries and car manufacturer Astra International pushed the Jakarta index up by the close on Monday, brokers said.
The index rose 2.27 points, or 0.40 percent, to close at 572.47 points after touching an intra-day low of 569.45 points in early trade. Losers led gainers by 54 to 51, with 59 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to be more active on Tuesday as bargain-hunters were targetting some heavyweights on perceptions that prices were low.

But brokers said the index would move in a narrow range as many investors were trading mostly on a short-term basis as they were awaiting upcoming Initital Public Offerings, including Daya Guna Samudra and Bank Negara Indonesia 1946 (BNI).
Fishery firm Daya Guna Samudra will be listed on October 24 while BNI, the country's largest state-owned bank, is to announce its offer price the same day.
Blue-chip cigarette company PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna surged in late trading following a weekend announcement that it had cancelled a shareholders meeting, brokers said.
It had risen 1,450 rupiah to 20,350 rupiah before closing at 20,250 rupiah on a volume of 1.3 million shares.

"It had attracted bargain-hunters since morning but a large number of buyers appeared in late trade. It is fuelled by the announcement that it has cancelled its November 2 shareholders meeting," said one foreign broker.
Brokers said many investors believed the company was to have put forward proposals to increase its holding in automobile manufacturer Astra International at the meeting.
The market had not reacted well to Sampoerna's announcement last month that a subsidiary had bought a 2.85 percent stake in Astra and talk that it could look to increase its holding.
Brokers said the cancellation could mean that Sampoerna had abandoned any such plan for now.

Astra was also actively traded following reports that a group linked to President Suharto had reached an agreement to buy a stake in the company from some state-owned bank and pension funds. It traded unchanged at 4,000 rupiah on a turnover of 1.5 million shares.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto, and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.
Secondliner property firm Bhuwanatala IP topped the active list with 14.3 million shares traded. It was unchanged at 1,700 rupiah after rising to 1,775 rupiah in early trade.
Brokers ascribed the activity to speculation of a possible link-up with a Singapore-based firm.
Company officials were not available immediately for comment.
